failures.title: Mercedes-Benz OM601 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch - 1983-1996 models
items.whatHappens: The single-row timing chain can stretch over high mileage, leading to a distinct rattling noise on cold starts. If ignored, it can jump a tooth, causing valve-to-piston contact and catastrophic engine failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, a timing chain kit replacement is straightforward and cost-effective. If the engine has already suffered valve damage, a full reconditioned unit is the only viable path.

items.title: Injector Seal Weeping - All variants
items.whatHappens: The copper washer seals at the base of the injectors degrade over time, allowing combustion gases to escape. This creates a black, crusty carbon buildup around the injector heads and can lead to difficult cold starts or rough idling.
items.repairVsReplace: This is a routine maintenance item, not a terminal failure. Replacing the seals and cleaning the head is inexpensive and should be done preventatively.

failures.goodYearsLine: The OM601 is widely regarded as one of Mercedes’ most robust four-cylinder diesels. Units maintained with regular oil changes routinely exceed 250,000 miles without major internal issues .

variants.title: OM601 Sub-Codes Explained - Which One Is in Your Car?
variants.intro: INTRO: The OM601 family shares the same fundamental block and head design, but displacement and tuning vary depending on the chassis and market. Identifying your exact sub-code ensures you order the correct injection pump and ancillary components. - Fitted to: 190-Class W201 (190D 2.0) - Key technical difference: The smallest displacement variant, featuring a specific 2.0L crankshaft and lighter flywheel. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; no unique widespread defects. - Interchange note: Not a straight swap with the 2.3L variants; the engine mounts, injection pump, and wiring loom differ significantly. - Fitted to: E-Class W124 (200D), T1 Vans (208D, 308D) - Key technical difference: Increased stroke to 2.3L for higher low-end torque, making it the preferred choice for light commercial applications. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above; commercial variants may experience earlier vacuum pump wear due to higher idle hours. - Interchange note: The passenger car and van versions share the same core block, but the sump, oil pickup, and accessory brackets are application-specific. - Fitted to: T1 Vans (308D, 408D), select export W124 models - Key technical difference: Functionally identical to the .940 in core architecture, but calibrated for specific regional emission standards or heavier van gross weights. - Sub-code-specific failure note: Shares the family failure pattern above. - Interchange note: Directly interchangeable with the OM601.940 in most van applications, provided the injection pump is swapped to match the original calibration.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement OM601 Engine - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used OM601 engine makes sense only if it comes with verifiable service history and a recent timing chain replacement. Given the age of these vehicles, the primary risk is hidden corrosion or degraded rubber seals, so a compression test is mandatory before purchase.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned OM601 engine is the sweet spot for most buyers. A reputable rebuild will address the common failure points by fitting a new timing chain kit, updated injector seals, and a refreshed mechanical injection pump, giving the engine a fresh lease on life.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full OM601 engine rebuild is justified for high-mileage commercial vans or classic 190D restorations where originality and maximum longevity are required. An upgraded rebuild should include line-boring the block, new pistons/rings, and a balanced crankshaft.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing and fitting through our vetted network ensures your OM601 engine is installed by specialists familiar with classic Mercedes mechanical diesels, backed by a nationwide warranty.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Because the OM601 is typically found in vehicles valued between £1,500 and £6,000, a full replacement can represent a significant portion of the car's worth. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing .

items.question: How much does a Mercedes OM601 engine replacement cost?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes OM601 engine typically costs between £1,200 and £1,800 for supply only . Fitted costs generally range from £1,800 to £2,500 depending on the specialist, while used units can be found from £400 but carry higher risk due to the engine's age. items.question: What is the most common failure on the OM601 engine?
items.answer: The most documented issues are timing chain stretch and injector seal weeping, often referred to as "Black Death". Timing chain rattle on cold starts is the primary warning sign of stretch, which can lead to catastrophic valve damage if ignored, whereas injector seal failure causes black carbon buildup around the injector heads and rough idling but is a cheap and routine fix. Get quotes for a rebuilt OM601 with these issues resolved

items.question: Which Mercedes models use the OM601 engine?
items.answer: The OM601 was fitted to the W201 190-Class (190D 2.0 and 2.2), the W124 E-Class (200D and 250D), and the T1/TN1 commercial vans (208D, 308D, 408D). It served as the backbone of Mercedes' compact and mid-size diesel range from 1983 to the late 1990s. Check your registration to confirm your exact OM601 fitment

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned OM601 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned OM601 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the age of these vehicles. A proper rebuild will replace the timing chain, tensioner, and injector seals, eliminating the two most common failure points, whereas used engines may appear cheaper upfront but often hide degraded rubber seals and stretched chains that will fail shortly after installation. Compare reconditioned OM601 engine prices from UK specialists

items.question: What is the difference between OM601.920, .940, and .950?
items.answer: The OM601.920 is the 2.0L variant (75 hp) found in the W201 190D, while the OM601.940 and .950 are 2.3L variants (79 hp). The .940 was used in passenger cars (W124) and some vans, while the .950 was calibrated for specific export or heavier van applications; they share the same core block, but the injection pumps, sumps, and accessory brackets are not always directly interchangeable without modification.
